title_en: Jiangsu Tianrong Group Co., Ltd. v. Hunan Haohua Chemical Co., Ltd. — dispute over unfair competition
ruling_gist_en: An English name that is actually used by a Chinese enterprise in foreign trade, corresponds to its Chinese enterprise name, and has acquired the function of identifying the market entity may be regarded as an 'enterprise name' within the meaning of Article 5(3) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China. The unauthorized use of another person's English enterprise name on exported goods, causing damage to that person, constitutes an act of unfair competition.
keywords_en: Civil; Unfair competition dispute; First instance; Basic People's Court; Jiangsu Province; Hunan Province; Legal person; Anti-Unfair Competition Law; Whether English enterprise names are protected under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law; Method for calculating damages; Unauthorized use of another's English enterprise name; Export of cartap technical material; Pesticide registration in India; Unfair competition; Unfair competition dispute of a limited liability company
full_text_en:
Jiangsu Tianrong Group Co., Ltd. v. Hunan Haohua Chemical Co., Ltd. — dispute over unfair competition

Ruling Summary

An English name that is actually used by a Chinese enterprise in foreign trade, corresponds to its Chinese company name, and has already acquired the function of identifying the business entity in the market, may be regarded as a "company name" within the meaning of Article 5(3) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China. Using another's English company name without authorization on exported goods, thereby causing harm to the other party, constitutes an act of unfair competition.

The amount of damages for unfair competition may be determined based on the losses suffered by the right holder as a result of the infringement during the period of infringement. The actual losses suffered by the right holder due to the infringement may be calculated as the product of the volume of infringing goods sold multiplied by the unit profit of the right holder's goods. Where the annual distribution of the sales volume of infringing goods is ascertainable, the calculation may be performed as the product of the annual sales volume of infringing goods multiplied by the right holder's unit profit for that year. The profit of the right holder's goods shall generally be calculated as operating profit, i.e., by deducting the corresponding selling expenses, administrative expenses, financial expenses, business taxes and surcharges from the sales profit.

Plaintiff: Jiangsu Tianrong Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Shugang Highway, Ecological Chemical Park, Xiangshui County, Yancheng City, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Xu Wangbao, Chairman of the Company.

Defendant: Hunan Haohua Chemical Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Dingshan Road, Shifeng District, Zhuzhou City, Hunan Province.
Legal Representative: Yuan Liang, General Manager of the Company.

The plaintiff, Jiangsu Tianrong Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianrong Company), filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court against the defendant, Hunan Haohua Chemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Haohua Company), over a dispute concerning the unauthorized use of another's enterprise name.

Plaintiff's Allegations:

On May 6, 2014, the Shanghai Pudong New Area Market Supervision Administration Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the Pudong Market Supervision Bureau) seized a total of 16,000 kg of cartap hydrochloride technical material (cartap TC) that the defendant intended to export to India, with a value of RMB 1,004,740.80. The packaging bags of the said cartap TC bore the plaintiff's English enterprise name "Jiangsu Tianrong Group Company Ltd., China." The Pudong Market Supervision Bureau imposed a penalty on the defendant for its illegal act. Cartap TC is a moderately toxic insecticide. Under Indian law, it may enter the Indian market only after obtaining official registration with the Indian authorities. The plaintiff's cartap TC had been registered with the Indian authorities, whereas the defendant's cartap TC had not. According to the customs declaration documents retained by Shanghai Customs, between June 2012 and January 2014, the defendant had used the plaintiff's English enterprise name without authorization to export 516,000 kg of cartap TC to India, with a value of USD 3,971,920. Calculated at the exchange rate of RMB 6.1565 per USD, this amounted to a total of RMB 24,453,125.48. By estimation, in 2014, the gross profit margin of the plaintiff's cartap TC was 42.62%. Based on this, the defendant's profit from exporting the goods in question totaled RMB 10,421,922.08. In addition, the plaintiff incurred legal fees of RMB 500,000 for this case. The defendant's unauthorized use of the plaintiff's enterprise name caused losses to the plaintiff and constituted unfair competition, for which the defendant should bear liability for damages.

Defendant's Defense:

The defendant had previously exported cartap TC to India through Sundat (S) PTE Ltd., Singapore. On this occasion, at the request of the Indian customer, the defendant used the plaintiff's English enterprise name on the packaging bags. These goods had been seized by the Pudong Market Supervision Bureau. The penalty imposed by the Pudong Market Supervision Bureau on the defendant was based on the Product Quality Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Product Quality Law"), not the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Anti-Unfair Competition Law"). The cartap TC packaging bags that the defendant had previously exported to India did not bear the plaintiff's English enterprise name; only the commercial invoices and packing lists for certain batches used the plaintiff's English enterprise name. The defendant's use of the plaintiff's English enterprise name was solely for the purpose of exporting, and did not cause the buyers to mistakenly believe that the goods in question were manufactured by the plaintiff, nor did it affect the plaintiff's exports, or cause any economic loss to the plaintiff. The plaintiff's English enterprise name had not been registered with the competent enterprise registration authority in accordance with the law, and therefore does not constitute an enterprise name protected under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. The defendant's conduct does not constitute unfair competition, and the plaintiff's claims lack factual and legal basis and should be dismissed. Even if the defendant's conduct constituted unfair competition, because the profit margin of the defendant's goods was very low and the profit was very small, the plaintiff's claimed amount of compensation and legal fees were both excessively high.

Facts Found by the Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court at First Instance:

I. Basic Information of the Plaintiff and the Defendant

The plaintiff Tianrong Company was established on September 29, 1998, with its registered business scope including the manufacture, processing, repackaging, and compounding of pesticides. The plaintiff's former enterprise name was Liyang Lihua Chemical Co., Ltd., which was changed to Jiangsu Lihua Chemical Co., Ltd. on March 4, 2003, to Jiangsu Tianrong Group Co., Ltd. on August 16, 2006, and to its current enterprise name on August 25, 2006.

The "Record of Registration for Foreign Trade Operator" of the plaintiff Tianrong Company shows that the English enterprise name it used when completing the registration of foreign trade operator with the relevant authorities on October 16, 2012, was "JIANGSU TIANRONG GROUP CO., LTD." A document issued by the Central Insecticides Board and Registration Committee of the Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine and Storage, Department of Agriculture and Cooperation, Ministry of Agriculture, Government of India, on October 9, 2015, stated that the plaintiff's cartap TC (minimum effective content 98%) had passed registration with the Indian government, and the plaintiff's English enterprise name was "JIANGSU TIANRONG GROUP CO., LTD."

The defendant Haohua Company was established on September 15, 2003, with its registered business scope including the processing of monosultap soluble powder, cartap hydrochloride soluble powder, processing of 40% omethoate emulsifiable concentrate, production of bisultap aqueous solution, production of monosultap technical material, and production of cartap hydrochloride technical material.

II. Circumstances of the Defendant's Use of the Plaintiff's English Enterprise Name in Exporting Cartap TC

On May 6, 2014, the Pudong Market Supervision Bureau seized 16,000 kg of cartap TC produced by the defendant Haohua Company, which was intended for export to India. The outer packaging of this batch of cartap TC bore the marking "Manufacturer: M/s. Liyang Chemical Factory, China (Jiangsu Tianrong Group Company, Ltd., China)." There were no other trademarks, enterprise names, or other identifiers on the packaging bags.

In a letter dated May 16, 2014, from the defendant Haohua Company to the Pudong Market Supervision Bureau, it stated: "On March 26, 2014, our company shipped one container of cartap TC totaling 16,000 kg to the Indian market. At the special request of the customer, the packaging bags of this batch of goods were printed with the factory name of the plaintiff Tianrong Company, which violated relevant regulations and caused a certain impact on the other party. Our company has engaged Crisher Company of India for registration since 2008. Due to the long cycle of Indian registration work, the registration certificate has not yet been obtained, and it is expected that registration can be obtained by the end of this year. Our company is willing to accept the administrative penalty imposed by your bureau, and at the same time earnestly requests your bureau to consider our company's specific practical difficulties and impose a lighter penalty as appropriate."

When Zhang Renjun, Deputy General Manager of the defendant Haohua Company, was questioned by the Pudong Market Supervision Bureau on June 19, 2014, he stated: Through an introduction, the defendant entered into a contract with Tobic (India) Limited on March 10, 2014, agreeing that the defendant would sell 16,000 kg of cartap TC to that Indian company. Indian law requires that official pesticide registration with the Indian authorities must be obtained before entering the Indian market for sale. Because the defendant had not obtained official Indian registration, while the plaintiff Tianrong Company had passed registration, in order to allow the defendant's cartap TC to pass through Indian customs, the defendant, at the request of the Indian customer, marked on the outer packaging of the goods "Manufacturer: M/s. Liyang Chemical Factory, China (Jiangsu Tianrong Group Company, Ltd., China)," which translated into Chinese means "Manufacturer: Liyang Chemical Factory, China (Jiangsu Tianrong Group Co., Ltd., China)." The packaging bags did not contain the defendant's name, marks, or related information. Third parties could not identify the goods in question as the defendant's products from the outer packaging alone. If an Indian customer saw the outer packaging of the goods in question, they would think they were the plaintiff's products. The defendant had been exporting pesticides to the Indian market for six or seven years. Previously, exports were made through Sundat (S) PTE Ltd., Singapore. That Singapore company had completed registration procedures in India, so its name was marked on the packaging.

Photographs on file with the Pudong Market Supervision Bureau show that the packaging bags of the plaintiff's 98% cartap TC contained both Chinese and English markings: "Jiangsu Tianrong Group Co., Ltd., China" and "JIANGSU TIANRONG GROUP CO., LTD, CHINA."

The Administrative Penalty Decision No. [2014] 150201402201, issued by the Pudong Market Supervision Bureau on July 5, 2014, states: The defendant Haohua Company is a state-owned enterprise engaged in the production and sale of pesticides. On March 10, 2014, the defendant entered into a contract with Tobic (India) Limited to sell 16,000 kg of cartap TC. On March 25, 2014, the defendant transported the above quantity of cartap TC to Shanghai Pudong, preparing to declare it for export to India. On May 6, 2014, based on a tip-off, the Pudong Market Supervision Bureau seized the 16,000 kg of cartap TC stored by the defendant at No. 66 Yanggao North First Road, Pudong New Area, Shanghai. The outer packaging bags of this batch of cartap TC bore the English enterprise name "Manufacturer: M/s. Liyang Chemical Factory, China (Jiangsu Tianrong Group Company, Ltd., China)." The outer packaging did not contain the defendant's name or related information, and was substantially identical to the English enterprise name "Jiangsu Tianrong Group Co. Ltd., China" on the outer packaging of the cartap TC exported to India by the plaintiff Tianrong Company. The value of this batch of goods was USD 163,200. Calculated at the RMB foreign exchange central parity rate of 1 USD to RMB 6.1565, published by the China Foreign Exchange Trade System authorized by the People's Bank of China on the date of the incident (May 6, 2014), as accepted by the party, the value was equivalent to RMB 1,004,740.80. On the date of the incident, the party completed the procedures for withdrawing the customs declaration, terminating the sales act. The Pudong Market Supervision Bureau determined that the defendant's use of the plaintiff's English enterprise name violated Articles 30 and 37 of the Product Quality Law, constituting the act of impersonating another's factory name. The Pudong Market Supervision Bureau ordered the defendant to correct the violation and imposed the following penalty: confiscation of 16,000 kg (640 bags) of cartap TC; and a fine of RMB 300,000.

In a statement dated July 9, 2014, issued by the defendant Haohua Company to the Pudong Market Supervision Bureau, it stated: The defendant received the Administrative Penalty Decision from the Pudong Market Supervision Bureau on July 9, 2014. The defendant has no objection to this and accepts the penalty decision. Because cartap TC has a shelf life, it requested the Pudong Market Supervision Bureau to dispose of the seized cartap TC promptly. On August 7, 2015, entrusted by the Pudong Market Supervision Bureau, Shanghai Maixun Auction Co., Ltd. auctioned the confiscated cartap TC, with the auction transaction price being RMB 402,000.

During the trial of this case, the court, upon the plaintiff Tianrong Company's application, obtained from Shanghai Customs the customs declaration materials for the defendant Haohua Company's export of cartap TC. According to the customs declaration materials provided by Shanghai Customs, between June 2012 and January 2014, the "Marks" column of the commercial invoices and packing lists for some batches of the defendant indicated the manufacturing enterprise name as the plaintiff's English enterprise name, while for other batches, it indicated "SUNDAT (S) PTE. LTD., SINGAPORE" (Sundat (S) PTE Ltd., Singapore). The plaintiff and defendant confirmed that the cartap TC for which the manufacturing enterprise name indicated on the commercial invoices and packing lists was the plaintiff's English enterprise name amounted to a total of USD 3,971,920, of which: USD 1,469,120 for 2012, USD 2,213,200 for 2013, and USD 289,600 for 2014. The plaintiff and defendant confirmed the calculation of RMB amounts at the exchange rate of RMB 6.1565 per USD.

III. Operational Circumstances of the Plaintiff and the Defendant

The audit report of the plaintiff Tianrong Company shows that its main products include the bisultap series, cartap hydrochloride series, fenoxaprop-p-ethyl herbicide series, and other herbicide series. (1) The audit report for fiscal year 2012 shows that for that year, operating revenue was RMB 199,980,695.72; operating cost was RMB 164,659,114.76; business taxes and surcharges were RMB 1,058.93; selling expenses, administrative expenses, and financial expenses totaled RMB 19,494,928.79; impairment loss on assets was RMB -950,400.80; operating profit was RMB 16,775,994.04. The average gross profit margin for main products was 17.73%, of which the cartap hydrochloride series had operating revenue of RMB 110,427,932.34, operating cost of RMB 87,794,178.03, and a gross profit margin of 20.50%. (2) The audit report for fiscal year 2013 shows that for that year, operating revenue was RMB 320,903,244.06; operating cost was RMB 249,155,948.20; business taxes and surcharges were RMB 780; selling expenses, administrative expenses, and financial expenses totaled RMB 40,642,405.65; impairment loss on assets was RMB 2,463,353.08; investment income was RMB 8,750,000; operating profit was RMB 37,390,757.13. The average gross profit margin for main products was 22.29%, of which the cartap hydrochloride series had operating revenue of RMB 173,867,734.11, operating cost of RMB 131,940,995.51, and a gross profit margin of 24.11%. (3) The audit report for fiscal year 2014 shows that for that year, operating revenue was RMB 457,960,940.49; operating cost was RMB 275,370,481.80; business taxes and surcharges were RMB 677,008.10; selling expenses, administrative expenses, and financial expenses were RMB 46,695,710.22; impairment loss on assets was RMB 49,615,505.45; operating profit was RMB 85,602,234.92. The average gross profit margin for main products was 39.80%, of which the cartap hydrochloride series had operating revenue of RMB 285,287,343.47, operating cost of RMB 160,960,977.95, and a gross profit margin of 43.58%. The audit report notes that the increase in gross profit margin for this year compared to the previous year is mainly due to the return to normal production after the company's relocation, with output becoming stable, a corresponding reduction in costs, an increase in selling prices in 2014, and a reduction in material costs.

The audit report of the defendant Haohua Company shows:

(1) For fiscal year 2012: total operating revenue was RMB 131,601,565.69; operating cost was RMB 105,897,551.31; operating profit was RMB -5,253,428.47. (2) For fiscal year 2013: total operating revenue was RMB 160,404,976.51; operating cost was RMB 131,995,080.08; operating profit was RMB 999,505.96. (3) For fiscal year 2014: total operating revenue was RMB 222,151,993.83; operating cost was RMB 150,655,163.02; operating profit was RMB 35,870,984.93. The defendant's audit report does not separately list the operating revenue and cost for cartap hydrochloride.

Additionally, it was found that the "Attorney Engagement Contract" signed between the plaintiff Tianrong Company (Party A) and Beijing Jincheng Tongda & Neal (Shanghai) Law Firm (Party B) stipulated that Party A engages Party B's lawyers to represent it in the unfair competition dispute case against the defendant Haohua Company. This case adopts a semi-contingent fee method for representation. The attorney's fee payable by Party A to Party B is as follows: (1) Fixed advance attorney's fees totaling RMB 500,000, with RMB 350,000 payable within one week of the contract's signing, and RMB 150,000 payable within one week after the final judgment (or the conclusion of the case by other means agreed in this contract). (2) Contingent attorney's fees based on the actual amount recovered from the defendant shall be paid by Party A to Party B as subsequent attorney's fees. The specific method is: 1. Within one week after Party A actually receives payment from the court or the opposing party, Party A shall settle with Party B for the contingent fee (subsequent attorney's fee) at 15% of the actual amount received, as remuneration for Party B's successful representation. 2. The actual amount received by Party A includes but is not limited to voluntary or self-performance by the opposing party, mediation, settlement, compulsory enforcement, etc., and the payments received include but are not limited to monetary payment, offset in kind, etc. On November 13, 2014, Beijing Jincheng Tongda & Neal (Shanghai) Law Firm issued an invoice for attorney's fees in the amount of RMB 350,000 to the plaintiff.

Opinion of the Court at First Instance: The Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court held as follows:

I. Whether the Defendant's Use of the Plaintiff's English Enterprise Name Constitutes Unfair Competition

Plaintiff Tianrong Company alleged that its English business name "JIANGSU TIANRONG GROUP CO., LTD" was a business name protected under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Defendant Haotian Company argued that, according to Article 6, Paragraph 1 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Cases of Unfair Competition*, the business names protected under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law were limited to three types: business names registered with the competent business registration authority; business names of foreign (regional) enterprises used commercially within China; and the trade names of business names that have a certain degree of market reputation and are known to the relevant public. The plaintiff's English business name had not been registered with the competent business registration authority, so it was not a business name protected under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. The court held that a business name was an important business identifier, through which the relevant public could identify the source of goods or services. A business name registered with the competent business registration authority typically included elements such as the name of the administrative division where the enterprise was located, the trade name, the industry or business characteristics, and the organizational form. In business activities, operators would not only use the full registered business name but also use the trade name, abbreviation, English business name, and other identifiers as needed. Article 6, Paragraph 1 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Cases of Unfair Competition* provided: "Business names registered with the competent business registration authority, as well as the business names of foreign (regional) enterprises used commercially within China, shall be recognized as 'business names' under Article 5, Item (3) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Trade names that have a certain degree of market reputation and are known to the relevant public may be recognized as 'business names' under Article 5, Item (3) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law." The judicial interpretation listed three types of business names, but this list was not exhaustive; it did not exclude other types of business names from the protection of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. For instance, the judicial interpretation did not include abbreviations of business names, but the ruling gist of Guiding Case No. 29 issued by the Supreme People's Court stated: "An abbreviation of a business name that has been used by an enterprise long-term and extensively, has a certain degree of market reputation, is known to the relevant public, and has actually functioned as a trade name may be deemed a business name and protected." Thus, the "business names" under Article 5, Item (3) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law were not limited to business names registered with the competent business registration authority. Although the Anti-Unfair Competition Law and its judicial interpretation did not explicitly provide that English business names could receive protection under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, it could not be inferred therefrom that English business names were not protected under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law.

Enterprises typically needed to use foreign language business names when engaging in foreign trade business activities. Article 9 of the *Foreign Trade Law of the People's Republic of China* provided that foreign trade operators engaged in the import or export of goods or technologies should register with the competent foreign trade department of the State Council or an agency authorized by it. The *Registration Form for Foreign Trade Operators* submitted by the plaintiff Tianrong Company to the relevant department for registration indicated its English business name as "JIANGSU TIANRONG GROUP CO., LTD," and the plaintiff also used this English business name when registering the Cartap pesticide it produced with the relevant Indian authorities. The court held that "Tianrong" was the plaintiff's trade name, "TIANRONG" was the pinyin of "Tianrong," "JIANGSU TIANRONG GROUP CO., LTD" corresponded to the plaintiff's Chinese business name, and the plaintiff actually used this English name in its business activities. This English business name had the function of identifying the market operator and was a "business name" under Article 5, Item (3) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, and was protected under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law.

Defendant Haohua Company argued that it only used the plaintiff Tianrong Company's English business name on the packaging bags of goods seized by the Pudong Market Supervision Bureau and did not use the plaintiff's English business name on the packaging bags of other goods sold to India. The court held that based on the following facts, it could be presumed that the defendant used the plaintiff's English business name on the outer packaging of goods when exporting Cartap to India from 2012 to 2014. First, because the defendant's Cartap had not been registered with the relevant Indian authorities, if the defendant had marked its own business name on the goods' packaging bags, its Cartap could not have entered the Indian market for sale. Second, in Case No. Pu Shi Jian An Chu Zi [2014] 150201402201, the defendant had used the plaintiff's English business name on the outer packaging of Cartap. Third, according to the customs declaration documents obtained by the court from Shanghai Customs upon the plaintiff's application, during the period from 2012 to 2014, the "marks and numbers" column of the commercial invoices and packing lists for some batches of Cartap exported by the defendant listed the plaintiff's English business name as the manufacturer, with a total value of USD 3,971,920. A commercial invoice was a price list issued by the exporter to the importer, serving as the basis for accounting between the buyer and seller and as a general statement for import and export customs declaration and tax payment. A packing list was a list detailing the packaging of exported goods. The contents of commercial invoices and packing lists should be consistent with the actual shipped goods. In the absence of contrary evidence, it could be determined that the defendant's packaging of those batches of Cartap bore the plaintiff's English business name.

Plaintiff Tianrong Company alleged that Defendant Haohua Company's unauthorized use of the plaintiff's English business name constituted unfair competition. The defendant argued that the goods in question were exported to the Indian market and would not cause confusion among the relevant domestic public or harm the plaintiff, so it did not constitute unfair competition. The court held that both the plaintiff and the defendant produced and sold Cartap, and both exported Cartap to India; there was a direct competitive relationship between them. The defendant used the plaintiff's English business name on the Cartap exported to India, had a subjective intent to imitate, objectively misled people into believing the goods were the plaintiff's goods, squeezed the plaintiff's export market share, and caused harm to the plaintiff. The defendant's conduct not only harmed the plaintiff's legitimate rights and interests but also disrupted the normal order of the foreign trade market. It constituted the unfair competition act of unauthorized use of another's business name under Article 5, Item (3) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law.

II. Regarding the Defendant's Liability for Compensation

According to Article 17, Paragraph 1 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Cases of Unfair Competition*, the amount of damages for unfair competition acts under Articles 5, 9, and 14 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law may be determined by reference to the method for determining damages for infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark. Article 56 of the *Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China* (as amended on October 27, 2001) provided that the amount of damages for infringement of the exclusive right to use a trademark shall be the profit gained by the infringer during the period of infringement due to the infringement, or the loss suffered by the infringed party during the period of infringement due to the infringement, including the reasonable expenses incurred by the infringed party to stop the infringement. Article 14 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Trademark Civil Disputes* provided that the profit gained by the infringer as referred to in Article 56, Paragraph 1 of the Trademark Law may be calculated as the product of the sales volume of the infringing goods and the unit profit of such goods; if the unit profit of such goods cannot be determined, it shall be calculated based on the unit profit of the registered trademark goods. Article 15 provided that the loss suffered by the infringed party as referred to in Article 56, Paragraph 1 of the Trademark Law may be calculated as the product of the reduction in sales of the right holder's goods caused by the infringement or the sales volume of the infringing goods and the unit profit of the registered trademark goods. By reference to the above provisions, the amount of damages in this case may be determined as the product of the sales volume of the infringing goods and the unit profit of such goods.

Plaintiff Tianrong Company argued that the amount of damages should be calculated based on the gross profit rate. Defendant Haohua Company argued that the gross profit rate had not deducted the expenses incurred in the enterprise's operations, so the damages should not be calculated based on the gross profit rate. The court held that an enterprise must pay corresponding taxes and incur corresponding expenses in its operations, and sales expenses, administrative expenses, and financial expenses typically accounted for a significant proportion of an enterprise's normal expenditures. Since gross profit is calculated without deducting business taxes and surcharges, sales expenses, administrative expenses, and financial expenses, there is generally a significant difference between an enterprise's gross profit and operating profit. Article 20 of the *Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Dispute Cases* provided that the profit gained by the infringer due to the infringement shall generally be calculated based on the infringer's operating profit; for an infringer whose sole business is infringement, the profit may be calculated based on sales profit. By reference to the above provisions, since the defendant in this case, in addition to producing and selling the infringing goods, also had other normal business operations, and the value of the goods involved in the case accounted for only a small portion of its operating revenue, the defendant was not an infringer whose sole business was infringement. Therefore, it was more reasonable to calculate the damages based on the operating profit rate.

Plaintiff Tianrong Company argued that the damages should be calculated by multiplying the plaintiff's profit rate for Cartap by the sales amount of the infringing goods. Defendant Haohua Company argued that the damages should be calculated by multiplying the defendant's profit rate for Cartap by the sales amount of the infringing goods. The court held that the defendant's annual audit reports only contained the profit statement for the entire company and did not separately list the operating revenue and operating costs for Cartap. Therefore, the profit rate for Cartap could not be calculated from the defendant's annual audit reports. The plaintiff's annual audit reports not only contained the company's profit statement but also separately listed the operating revenue and operating costs for Cartap, from which the plaintiff's profit rate for Cartap could be generally calculated. Since the unit profit of the defendant's Cartap could not be determined, the damages could be calculated based on the unit profit of the plaintiff's Cartap.

The plaintiff Tianrong Company's annual audit reports contained the operating revenue and operating costs for Cartap. When calculating the operating profit for Cartap, the corresponding business taxes and surcharges, sales expenses, administrative expenses, and financial expenses should also be deducted in proportion to the ratio of Cartap's operating revenue to the enterprise's total operating revenue. The operating profit rate for Cartap = [Operating revenue of Cartap - Operating cost of Cartap - (Business taxes and surcharges + Sales expenses + Administrative expenses + Financial expenses) × (Operating revenue of Cartap / Total operating revenue)] / Operating revenue of Cartap. Taking fiscal year 2012 as an example, the plaintiff's operating revenue was RMB 199,980,695.72, operating cost was RMB 164,659,114.76, total business taxes and surcharges, sales expenses, administrative expenses, and financial expenses were RMB 19,495,987.72, operating revenue of Cartap was RMB 110,427,932.34, and operating cost of Cartap was RMB 87,794,178.03. According to the above formula, the operating profit rate for the plaintiff's Cartap in that year was 10.75%. Using the same formula, the operating profit rate for the plaintiff's Cartap in fiscal year 2013 was 11.45%, and in fiscal year 2014 was 33.24%.

The value of the Cartap technical material exported by Defendant Haohua Company using the plaintiff Tianrong Company's English business name was USD 3,971,920, of which USD 1,469,120 was in 2012, USD 2,213,200 in 2013, and USD 289,600 in 2014. Multiplying the value of the defendant's exported Cartap in each year by the plaintiff's profit rate for Cartap in that year, and converting at an exchange rate of USD 1 = RMB 6.1565, the operating profits for the infringing goods involved in the case from 2012 to 2014 were RMB 972,298.51, RMB 1,560,127.28, and RMB 592,643.41, respectively, totaling RMB 3,125,069.20. The defendant should also bear the reasonable attorney fees incurred by the plaintiff for this case. The plaintiff claimed attorney fees of RMB 500,000, which the court considered excessive. The court determined the attorney fees to be RMB 200,000, taking into account factors such as the amount in dispute, the amount of the award, the complexity of the case, the workload of the attorneys, and relevant attorney fee standards.

In conclusion, the Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court, in accordance with Article 5, Item (3) and Article 20 of the *Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China*, and Article 17, Paragraph 1 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Cases of Unfair Competition*, rendered the following judgment on November 10, 2016:

1. Defendant Haohua Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate Plaintiff Tianrong Company for economic losses in the amount of RMB 3,125,069.20;
2. Defendant Haohua Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate Plaintiff Tianrong Company for the attorney fees incurred to stop the unfair competition act in the amount of RMB 200,000.

After the first-instance judgment, neither party filed an appeal within the statutory period, and the first-instance judgment has become legally effective.
